# Research

I use quantitative and computational methods to investigate social and policy questions, working across textual, survey, administrative and other forms of social data.

My research interests have developed across development research and programme evaluation, applied policy analysis, and computational social science. Across these settings, I am particularly interested in how data and quantitative methods can be used to measure social phenomena, understand patterns in public discourse, and generate evidence for policy and programme decisions.

## Computational social science

My current research interests focus on computational approaches to social and political questions, particularly the analysis of online discourse and public opinion.

My MSc dissertation at Trinity College Dublin examined public sentiment and hate speech in discussions about immigration in Ireland using Reddit data. The project combined quantitative text analysis, sentiment analysis, supervised machine learning and topic modelling to investigate how immigration discourse has changed over time and what themes characterise potentially hateful content.

I have also applied computational text analysis to political speech, analysing Indian Union Budget speeches over several decades using lexical, readability and sentiment measures.

## Applied policy and administrative data

I have worked with administrative and assessment data to investigate social and policy questions where individual-level evidence can inform institutional decision-making.

At the Injuries Resolution Board, I contributed to research examining accidents involving cyclists and e-scooter users, combining quantitative analysis of injury and accident characteristics with thematic analysis of qualitative information from medical reports.

I also worked on analysis of personal injury compensation assessments, examining award values, claim volumes, injury characteristics and changes over time.

## Development research and programme evaluation

Before moving into academic social data science, I worked extensively in development research, programme evaluation and evidence generation.

My work included research on women's empowerment, market access, digital and financial inclusion, nutrition, and programme implementation. At Grameen Foundation, I contributed to the measurement and evaluation of development programmes, including the MANDI project in Uttar Pradesh, which examined women's empowerment and market inclusion using quantitative and qualitative approaches.

This work shaped my interest in measurement: how abstract social concepts such as empowerment, agency and inclusion can be operationalised, measured and evaluated using empirical data.

## Quantitative methods

A recurring strand of my work is the application and communication of quantitative methods for social research.

I have worked with multivariate methods including Multiple Correspondence Analysis and Geometric Data Analysis, statistical modelling, machine learning, quantitative text analysis and data visualisation.

My work using MCA and GDA examined patterns of religious beliefs and their relationship to social characteristics, while other projects have used text analysis and machine learning to study political speeches and online public discourse.
